name: emit
description: Decides the next bead-action changeset deterministically. Pure function over the impact report, .bead-map.json, the spec directory, and a caller-supplied git HEAD SHA. Emits changeset.json — an ordered, tool-agnostic list of label/create/close/tag operations with forward-reference encoding — that an external adapter consumes.

requirements.title: Pure function over inputs
requirements.description: spex emit reads the impact report (stdin or --impact), .bead-map.json, the spec directory, and the --git-head SHA; writes changeset.json to stdout. No subprocess invocations, no live tracker calls, no git calls. Given identical inputs, always produces byte-identical changeset output.

requirements.title: Topological ordering within type levels
requirements.description: Ops are emitted in an order that respects type tiers (proposal epic first, then features and data_flow tasks, then multi-component test tasks) and respects spec-graph dependencies within each tier. When new bead B depends on new bead A, A's create op comes before B's, so the adapter can build A first and forward-resolve B's dep at exec time. Same-tier ties break deterministically by spec_node_id.

requirements.title: Priority propagation through project requirements
requirements.description: Each create op carries a priority derived from the chain component.implements → module_requirement.preq_id → project_requirement.priority. Lowest numeric priority wins across the implements set. Passed through in the op's priority field for the adapter to forward to the tracker.

requirements.title: Parent resolution from mapping store
requirements.description: Each create op's parent field encodes the proposal epic for the run. The epic is either the op_id of a same-run epic create (first op) or a bead_id ref to a pre-existing epic. All non-epic creates in the run parent under this single epic reference.

requirements.title: Forward-reference encoding for in-batch creates
requirements.description: Parent and dependency fields use three ref shapes: {"ref":"bead","bead_id":"<id>"} for existing beads; {"ref":"op","op_id":"<id>"} for the result of another create op in the same changeset; {"ref":"spec_node","spec_node_id":"<id>"} for adapter-time lookup against the mapping store. Resolving DepSpecNodeIDs from impact into these three shapes is how emit fixes the broken-dep-graph bug: same-run deps become op refs resolved by the adapter at exec time rather than pre-resolved stale bead IDs.

requirements.title: Idempotency label construction
requirements.description: Each create op carries an idempotency.label field of the form spex:<record-id> where record-id is the next integer ID the ingest reconciler will assign. The adapter matches this label against the tracker before creating; a pre-existing match produces a was_existing=true skipped receipt rather than a duplicate bead. Record IDs come from the mapping store's monotonic counter.

requirements.title: Git HEAD threaded from caller
requirements.description: emit accepts --git-head <sha> and embeds the SHA into changeset.json under the top-level git_head field. The adapter uses this value to build commit:<HEAD> labels on obsoleted beads. spex never calls git rev-parse; the caller supplies $(git rev-parse HEAD) from their shell.

requirements.title: Deterministic changeset schema
requirements.description: changeset.json carries a top-level "version": 1 field. The schema is stable across runs: op ordering is deterministic, all ref shapes use named fields, field order is canonical so two runs with identical inputs produce byte-identical output suitable for git diff review.

requirements.title: Tool-agnostic operation vocabulary
requirements.description: Operations are label, create, close, and tag — abstract over any bead tracker. No tracker-specific flags or subcommand names appear in changeset.json. Adapters for br, bd, GitHub Issues, or Jira consume the same vocabulary.

components.name: ChangesetBuilder
components.description: Composes changeset.json from the impact report, mapping store records, spec graph, and caller-supplied git HEAD. Delegates dep resolution to Resolver, op ordering to TopologicalSorter, and idempotency labels to IdempotencyLabeler. Writes the final v1 changeset with canonical field order.

components.name: Resolver
components.description: Resolves each create action's DepSpecNodeIDs and parent_spec_node_id into the three ref shapes. Classifies each dep: if another op in the same batch targets the spec_node_id → ref:op; else if the mapping store has an open bead → ref:bead; else → ref:spec_node (adapter-time fallback). Also computes priority by walking component.implements → module_requirement.preq_id → project_requirement.priority and taking the minimum.

components.name: TopologicalSorter
components.description: Orders the create ops so every in-batch dep comes before its dependent. Uses Kahn's algorithm over the (create op, DepSpecNodeIDs → op_id) DAG restricted to the current batch. Detects cycles and returns an error (a cycle in spec-graph deps within one batch is a spec error, not an emit error). Secondary sort key: spec_node_id lex order, for determinism on unconstrained pairs.

components.name: IdempotencyLabeler
components.description: Assigns each create op its idempotency.label in the form spex:<record-id>. The record-id is the next integer from the mapping store's monotonic counter, reserved at emit time so ingest's later reconciliation uses the same value. Never reuses a record-id across runs.

components.name: EmitCommand
components.description: CLI entry point: spex emit --proposal <ref> --git-head <sha> [--impact <file>] [--out <file>]. Reads the impact report (stdin or --impact), loads .bead-map.json via the map module, loads the spec graph, wires ChangesetBuilder, writes changeset.json to stdout or --out.

data_flows.name: Emit flow
data_flows.description: Impact report + .bead-map.json + spec graph + git HEAD → Resolver classifies each create's refs → TopologicalSorter orders ops → IdempotencyLabeler assigns labels → ChangesetBuilder composes and writes changeset.json v1.
